owner: xlog baseline — mainstream shorts conventions + pilot creator reference (LoL commentary style)

criteria.name: hook_strength
criteria.description: The opening must stop the scroll immediately: cold-open on the highest-action moment with no title card or pre-roll, and land the first caption line within the first ~0.5s as an unresolved claim that only completes in the next line. Judged over the first 3 seconds.

criteria.name: mainstream_convention
criteria.description: Follows proven, broadly appealing Shorts/Reels conventions for caption placement, structure, and readability. Safe beats experimental — except that the creator's reference establishes narration-subtitle-driven, letterboxed gameplay commentary as an accepted house form; do not penalize long uncut takes or 16:9-in-9:16 letterboxing on their own.

criteria.name: instruction_fit
criteria.description: Faithfully realizes the user's free-form request (caption tone, effects, mood). Ignore this criterion (redistribute judgment) when no request was given.

criteria.name: pacing
criteria.description: No dead air and energy rising toward the payoff. Perceived pace may come from subtitle turnover (one short line every 1–2s) over long uncut takes rather than from frequent hard cuts; deliberate rhythm breaks (e.g., a mid-roll still interlude) are welcome when they set up a payoff.

criteria.name: narrative_clarity
criteria.description: One clear thread from hook to payoff; no confusing jumps. Silent visual interludes are fine when they restate the narration's point rather than introduce a new one.

criteria.name: moment_selection
criteria.description: The genuinely best raw moments were used, not filler.

preferences: Open cold on the highest-action moment of the clip and place the first subtitle line within the first 0.5 seconds, phrased as an incomplete claim that only resolves in the next line.
Keep gameplay in long uncut takes and generate pace with subtitle turnover instead of cuts — swap one short caption line every 1–2 seconds, one spoken clause per line.
Burn captions as bold white text on a soft dark translucent plate, centered in the lower third and above the game HUD, never covering the minimap or item bar.
Letterbox the 16:9 gameplay in a 9:16 frame and keep the crop centered on the champion so the black bars double as caption space.
Insert one silent full-bleed meme/still interlude around the 55–70% mark that visually restates the narration's joke, holding each still 2–3 seconds.
Join interlude stills with 0.5–1s dip-to-black fades rather than hard cuts, and drop all captions during the interlude so the image carries the gag.
Drop captions during the peak action beat so the payoff can breathe.
End on a short self-deprecating reaction caption over live action and fade to black mid-play instead of using an outro card.
Avoid emojis and on-screen title cards.
notes: v2 — merged the pilot creator's reference style: https://youtube.com/shorts/eWQMnGwj0Cg?si=yT5F1SphInJPgJRL (Korean LoL gameplay commentary short). Learned: the creator's house style is narration-subtitle-driven rather than cut-driven — letterboxed 16:9 gameplay in long uncut takes, bold white captions on a translucent plate in the lower third above the HUD swapping every 1–2s, a cold open with the first line inside 0.5s as an unresolved hook, one silent full-bleed meme-still interlude mid-roll (stills held 2–3s, joined by 0.5–1s dip-to-black fades, no captions) as a visual punchline, and a close on a self-deprecating caption fading to black mid-action with no outro card. Criterion edits: hook_strength now specifies the cold open and sub-second first caption; pacing no longer requires frequent hard cuts and accepts subtitle turnover plus deliberate rhythm breaks; mainstream_convention now exempts letterboxing and long takes from the 'safe over experimental' penalty; narrative_clarity clarifies that silent interludes must restate, not extend, the thread. Weights unchanged.
